text: A hotel books a housekeeper for a morning shift, and pays up front.
Or someone accepts it, and never shows up.
For the first, every booking has a timer in the cloud, set for its start time.
If nobody has accepted by then, the booking cancels itself and the money goes back.
When I came back to it later, I found an accepted job that never started just stayed open, with the hotel's money held.
So I added a no-show rule.
When a provider accepts, a second timer is set for the end of the shift, plus a grace period.
If the job never started, the booking is cancelled and refunded.
Nobody gets a strike for it, because nobody chose to cancel.
One more catch: the cloud's task service won't schedule anything more than thirty days ahead.
So a timer for a booking further out wakes at twenty-nine days, sees it's early, and sets itself again.
No booking can get stuck, and nobody has to watch the clock.
